description:
A markdown notes editor where every keystroke is durable and saving is export.

Continuity is a native Win32 markdown notes editor for Windows. Every keystroke is written to a local SQLite database, so saving a file is an export rather than a durability step. Markdown source stays canonical while a live renderer projects headings, lists, checkboxes, links, tables, inline code, and images in place.
It supports multi-pane and multi-tab session restore, vault folders with autosave, spreadsheet-style pipe-table editing, configurable themes and keymaps, and a portable mode that keeps settings, notes, and backups beside the executable.
- Clicking back into a window or a split pane no longer jumps the view somewhere else. Whenever the window's layout was refreshed - clicking into a pane after a split or resize, resizing the window, toggling the sidebar - Continuity re-centred the view on the caret, so if you had scrolled away from the caret to read another part of the note, the view snapped back to wherever the caret happened to be (often the top or bottom of the document). The view now stays exactly where you left it; the caret only stays pinned in place when it is actually on screen.
